result.question: Why did David’s men swear that he must never again go out with them to battle?

readings.answer: To keep the lamp of Israel from being extinguished
readings.support: so that the lamp of Israel may not be extinguished

readings.answer: Because his life was in danger and he had to be rescued
readings.support: resolved to kill David | came to his aid

assessments.reason: It restates the passage’s explicit purpose clause: “so that the lamp of Israel may not be extinguished.”

The text shows David’s life was threatened and he was rescued just before the oath, making his endangerment a plausible motive, though the stated reason given is the lamp-of-Israel not being extinguished.
While David was exhausted, the passage does not give this as the reason for the oath; it explicitly says they swore so the lamp of Israel would not be extinguished.
